```{r data_setup}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(here)

set.seed(42)  # global random seed

# --- LOAD AND JOIN CSVs -------------------------------------------------------

# Read both CSV files
values_raw <- read_csv(here("data", "raw", "train_values.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE)

labels_raw <- read_csv(here("data", "raw", "train_labels.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE)

# Join as tibble
data <- values_raw |>
  inner_join(labels_raw, by = "building_id", relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  as_tibble()

# Throws an error if any rows are dropped
stopifnot(nrow(data) == nrow(values_raw))

# Save to "data/processed" for further processing and modeling
saveRDS(data, here("data", "processed", "earthquake.rds"))
```

```{r preprocessing}

# --- PREPROCESSING ------------------------------------------------------------

# Load the full (joined) dataset
data <- readRDS(here("data", "processed", "earthquake.rds"))

# Convert outcome to a labeled categorical factor
data <- data |>
  mutate(
    damage_grade = factor(
      damage_grade, 
      levels = c(3, 2, 1), 
      labels = c("high", "medium", "low"),
      ordered = TRUE
    )
  )

# Convert other categoricals to factors
data <- data |>
  mutate(across(c(where(is_character), geo_level_1_id), as.factor))


# --- SPLITS -------------------------------------------------------------------

eq_split <- initial_split(data, prop = 0.80, strata = damage_grade)
train_data <- training(eq_split)
test_data  <- testing(eq_split)

# 5-fold stratified CV
folds <- vfold_cv(train_data, v = 5, strata = damage_grade)


# --- RECIPE -------------------------------------------------------------------

base_recipe <- recipe(damage_grade ~ ., data = train_data) |>
  update_role(building_id, new_role = "id") |>
  step_rm(has_secondary_use, geo_level_2_id, geo_level_3_id) |>
  step_novel(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = FALSE) |>  # no one_hot prevents multicollinearity
  step_zv(all_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())
```

# Elastic Net — Gina Mancuso

The elastic-net work is organized into three scripts so that the leakage-safe
geographic encoding can be reused and the final candidate remains separate
from the ordinal sensitivity analysis:

- `models/mancuso_geography_helpers.R` defines fold-safe class weights,
  smoothed geographic encodings, preprocessing, and evaluation metrics.
- `models/mancuso_geographic_elastic_net_candidate.R` fits the locked
  multinomial candidate using five-fold stratified cross-validation.
- `models/mancuso_ordinal_elastic_net_experiment.R` evaluates an explicitly
  ordinal alternative as a training-only sensitivity analysis.

The candidate uses moderate square-root inverse-frequency class weights,
smoothed encodings of `geo_level_2_id` and `geo_level_3_id`, a penalty of
0.003, a mixture of 0.50, and geographic smoothing strength of 10. All
outcome-informed transformations are estimated inside each analysis fold and
then applied to its assessment fold. The final holdout is not accessed unless
`evaluate_holdout` is deliberately changed from `FALSE` in the candidate
script.

## Reproducing the elastic-net analyses

The following calls are intentionally not executed during routine rendering
because they refit the models. The complete implementation is retained in the
referenced scripts rather than duplicated inside this group document.

```{r elastic_net_final_candidate}
#| eval: false

source(here("models", "mancuso_geographic_elastic_net_candidate.R"))
```

```{r elastic_net_ordinal_sensitivity}
#| eval: false

source(here("models", "mancuso_ordinal_elastic_net_experiment.R"))
```

These tables contain out-of-fold predictions from the training set. They are
not final holdout results.

```{r elastic_net_saved_results}
elastic_net_overall <- read_csv(
  here("results", "metrics", "elastic_net_geographic_candidate_oof_metrics.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

elastic_net_by_class <- read_csv(
  here("results", "metrics", "elastic_net_geographic_candidate_oof_per_class.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

elastic_net_parameters <- read_csv(
  here("results", "metrics", "elastic_net_geographic_candidate_parameters.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

elastic_net_overall
elastic_net_by_class
elastic_net_parameters
```

The selected multinomial candidate achieved QWK = 0.6125, accuracy = 0.7249,
macro F1 = 0.6857, and macro recall = 0.6984. The ordinal sensitivity model
achieved a lower QWK of 0.6019 and did not improve QWK in any of the five
paired validation folds, so the multinomial formulation was retained.

## Model

```{r}

  set_engine("nnet") |>
  set_mode("classification")

log_reg_workflow <- workflow() |>
  add_model(multinomial_spec) |>
  add_recipe(base_recipe)
```

## Cross-validation

```{r}
#| label: cv-fit
set.seed(123)
log_reg_resamples <- fit_resamples(
  log_reg_workflow,
  resamples = folds,
  metrics = grade_metrics,
  control = control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE)
)

cv_metrics <- collect_metrics(log_reg_resamples)
cv_metrics
```

### Per-class CV metrics

Precision, recall, and F1 for each damage grade use pooled out-of-fold predictions from the shared folds.

```{r}
#| label: per-class-cv
cv_pred <- collect_predictions(log_reg_resamples)
cm_tbl <- conf_mat(cv_pred, damage_grade, estimate = .pred_class)$table

cv_per_class <- map_dfr(rownames(cm_tbl), function(cls) {
  tp <- cm_tbl[cls, cls]
  fp <- sum(cm_tbl[cls, ]) - tp
  fn <- sum(cm_tbl[, cls]) - tp
  tibble(
    class = cls,
    precision = tp / (tp + fp),
    recall = tp / (tp + fn),
    f_meas = 2 * tp / (2 * tp + fp + fn)
  )
})

cv_per_class
```

### Save CV results

```{r}
#| label: save-cv-results
#| include: false
metrics_dir <- here("results", "metrics")
dir.create(metrics_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

cv_metrics |>
  mutate(model = "multinomial_logistic") |>
  write_csv(file.path(metrics_dir, "chang_multinomial_logistic_cv.csv"))

cv_per_class |>
  mutate(model = "multinomial_logistic") |>
  write_csv(file.path(metrics_dir, "chang_multinomial_logistic_cv_per_class.csv"))
```

## Baseline Cross-Validation

```{r}
model_xgb <- boost_tree(mode = "classification",
  trees = 100, learn_rate = 0.1, tree_depth = 3) |>
  set_engine("xgboost", nthread = 1)

workflow_xgb <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(base_recipe) |>
  add_model(model_xgb)

set.seed(42)
xgb_fit_cv <- workflow_xgb |>
  fit_resamples(resamples = folds, metrics = model_metrics)
xgb_baseline_metrics <- collect_metrics(xgb_fit_cv)
xgb_baseline_metrics
```

## Weighting

```{r}
weight_exponent <- 0.5
class_counts <- train_data |>
  count(damage_grade, name = "class_count")
weighted_train <- train_data |>
  left_join(class_counts, by = "damage_grade") |>
  mutate(case_weight = (nrow(train_data) / class_count)^weight_exponent,
    case_weight = hardhat::importance_weights(case_weight / mean(case_weight))) |>
  select(-class_count)

weighted_splits <- vector("list", nrow(folds))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(folds))) 
{
  split <- folds$splits[[i]]
  analysis_data <- analysis(split)
  class_counts <- analysis_data |>
    count(damage_grade, name = "class_count")
  analysis_data <- analysis_data |>
    left_join(class_counts, by = "damage_grade") |>
    mutate(case_weight = (nrow(analysis_data) / class_count)^weight_exponent,
      case_weight = hardhat::importance_weights(case_weight / mean(case_weight))) |>
    select(-class_count)
  assessment_data <- assessment(split) |>
    mutate(case_weight = hardhat::importance_weights(rep(1, n())))
  n_analysis <- nrow(analysis_data)
  weighted_splits[[i]] <- make_splits(list(analysis = seq_len(n_analysis),
    assessment = n_analysis + seq_len(nrow(assessment_data))),
    data = bind_rows(analysis_data, assessment_data))
}
weighted_folds <- manual_rset(weighted_splits, ids = folds$id)

weighted_recipe <- recipe(damage_grade ~ ., data = weighted_train) |>
  update_role(building_id, new_role = "id") |>
  step_rm(has_secondary_use, geo_level_2_id, geo_level_3_id) |>
  step_novel(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = FALSE) |>
  step_zv(all_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())
```

```{r}
initial_candidates <- 15

model_xgb_tune <- boost_tree(mode = "classification", trees = tune(),
  learn_rate = tune(), tree_depth = tune(), min_n = tune(),
  loss_reduction = tune(), sample_size = tune(), mtry = tune()) |>
  set_engine("xgboost", nthread = 1, counts = FALSE)

workflow_xgb_tune <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(weighted_recipe) |>
  add_model(model_xgb_tune) |>
  add_case_weights(case_weight)

parameters_xgb <- extract_parameter_set_dials(workflow_xgb_tune) |>
  update(trees = trees(c(100, 1500)),
    learn_rate = learn_rate(log10(c(0.01, 0.20))),
    tree_depth = tree_depth(c(2, 14)),
    min_n = min_n(c(2, 30)),
    loss_reduction = loss_reduction(c(0, 5), trans = NULL),
    sample_size = sample_prop(c(0.6, 1.0)),
    mtry = mtry_prop(c(0.3, 1.0)))

set.seed(42)
initial_grid <- grid_space_filling(parameters_xgb,
  size = initial_candidates, type = "latin_hypercube")
initial_grid
```

## Tuning Test

```{r}
set.seed(42)
xgb_initial_results <- workflow_xgb_tune |>
  tune_grid(resamples = weighted_folds, grid = initial_grid,
    metrics = model_metrics, control = control_grid(verbose = TRUE))
```

```{r}
bayes_iterations <- 25
control_xgb_bayes <- control_bayes(
  verbose = TRUE, verbose_iter = TRUE, no_improve = 10,
  seed = 42, parallel_over = "resamples")

set.seed(42)
xgb_tune_results <- workflow_xgb_tune |>
  tune_bayes(resamples = weighted_folds, initial = xgb_initial_results,
    param_info = parameters_xgb, iter = bayes_iterations,
    metrics = model_metrics, control = control_xgb_bayes)
```

## Cross-Validation Results

```{r}
xgb_tuned_metrics <- xgb_tuning_metrics |>
  filter(.config == best_xgb_parameters$.config) |>
  select(.metric, .estimator, mean, n, std_err)

xgb_cv_comparison <- bind_rows(xgb_baseline_metrics |> mutate(model = "Unweighted baseline"),
  xgb_tuned_metrics |> mutate(model = "Mild-weighted Bayesian (depth 2–14)")) |>
  select(model, .metric, mean, std_err)

xgb_cv_comparison |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = .metric, values_from = c(mean, std_err))
```


```{r}
baseline_folds <- collect_metrics(xgb_fit_cv, summarize = FALSE) |>
  select(id, .metric, baseline = .estimate)

tuned_folds <- collect_metrics(xgb_tune_results, summarize = FALSE) |>
  filter(.config == best_xgb_parameters$.config) |>
  select(id, .metric, tuned = .estimate)

xgb_fold_comparison <- baseline_folds |>
  inner_join(tuned_folds, by = c("id", ".metric")) |>
  mutate(change = tuned - baseline)

xgb_fold_comparison |>
  group_by(.metric) |>
  summarise(mean_change = mean(change), folds_improved = sum(change > 0), folds_declined = sum(change < 0), .groups = "drop")
```

# Random Forest
```{r}
# tidymodels and data management
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(here)

# parallelization
library(future)
library(doFuture)
library(future.callr) # More robust backend for Positron

# Setup ------------------------------------------------------------------------
message("Executing Random Forest pipeline.")

set.seed(42)
processed_path <- here("data", "processed", "earthquake.rds")
split_path <- here("data", "processed", "split_data.RData")

if (!file.exists(processed_path)) {
  source(here("shared", "01_data_setup.R"))
}

if (!file.exists(split_path)) {
  source(here("shared", "02_preprocessing.R"))
}

load(split_path)

# Increase the export memory limit to 2 GB to handle the large dataset
options(future.globals.maxSize = 2000 * 1024^2)

# Detect number of usable cores (leaving one for OS processes)
total_cores <- max(1, parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE) - 1)
registerDoFuture()

# We have 5 folds, so we never need more than 5 parallel workers during tuning
cv_workers <- min(5, total_cores)
worker_threads <- max(1, floor(total_cores / cv_workers))

# Use callr instead of multisession to bypass socket connection errors
plan(callr, workers = cv_workers)
message(paste("Active parallel workers:", nbrOfWorkers()))
message(sprintf("Assigned %d threads per worker.", worker_threads))


# Model Specification ----------------------------------------------------------

# Define class weights based on their inverse frequencies
rf_class_weights <- train_data |>
  count(damage_grade) |>
  mutate(weight = sum(n) / n) |> 
  arrange(damage_grade) |> 
  pull(weight)

# Initialize the model
base_rf_spec <- rand_forest(
  mtry  = tune(),
  trees = 100,    # small number of trees for tuning, will increase at final fit
  min_n = tune()
) |> set_mode("classification")

# Inject the weights so workers receive the raw numbers
rf_spec <- rlang::inject(
  set_engine(
    base_rf_spec,
    "ranger",
    num.threads   = worker_threads,
    importance    = "impurity",
    class.weights = !!rf_class_weights 
  )
)

# Tidymodels Workflow and Setup ------------------------------------------------
rf_wf <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(base_recipe) |>
  add_model(rf_spec)

rf_params <- extract_parameter_set_dials(rf_wf) |>
  update(
    mtry  = mtry(range = c(5, 85)),
    min_n = min_n(range = c(5, 50))
  )

# Metrics & Controls -----------------------------------------------------------
qwk <- metric_tweak("qwk", kap, weighting = "quadratic")
f_micro <- metric_tweak("f_micro", f_meas, estimator = "micro")
custom_metrics <- metric_set(qwk, f_micro, accuracy)

ctrl_bayes <- control_bayes(
  save_pred     = TRUE,
  verbose       = TRUE,
  no_improve    = 10,
  seed          = 42,
  parallel_over = "resamples"
)


### Replaced with Bayesian hyperparameter optimization
####################################################
# ctrl_grid <- control_grid(
#   save_pred     = TRUE,
#   parallel_over = "everything"
# )

# Grid Search ------------------------------------------------------------------
# message("Executing Space-Filling Grid Search...")
# rf_grid_results <- tune_grid(
#   rf_wf,
#   resamples = folds,
#   grid      = grid_space_filling(rf_params, size = 15),
#   metrics   = custom_metrics,
#   control   = ctrl_grid
# )

# saveRDS(rf_grid_results, here("results", "metrics", "rf_grid_results.rds"))
####################################################


# Bayesian Tuning --------------------------------------------------------------
message("Tuning parameters...")
rf_bayes_results <- tune_bayes(
  rf_wf,
  resamples  = folds,
  param_info = rf_params,
  initial    = 5,
  iter       = 10,
  metrics    = custom_metrics,
  control    = ctrl_bayes
)

saveRDS(rf_bayes_results, here("results", "metrics", "rf_bayes_results.rds"))

# Final Fit --------------------------------------------------------------------
# Clean up parallelization to maximize final training efficiency
plan(sequential)
registerDoSEQ()

best_params <- select_best(rf_bayes_results, metric = "qwk")

# Update model to 1000 trees for final fit
final_rf_spec <- rlang::inject(
  rf_spec |> 
    update(trees = 1000) |> 
    set_engine("ranger",
      num.threads   = total_cores,    # allocate all available cores for
      importance    = "impurity",     #   training, leaving one for OS
      class.weights = !!rf_class_weights)
)

# Finalize workflow with final model specification and tuned parameters
final_rf_wf <- rf_wf |> 
  update_model(final_rf_spec) |>
  finalize_workflow(best_params)

# Manually train on full training data and evaluate on test data
final_fit_model <- fit(final_rf_wf, data = train_data)
final_preds <- augment(final_fit_model, new_data = test_data)
final_metrics   <- custom_metrics(final_preds, truth = damage_grade, estimate = .pred_class)

saveRDS(final_fit_model, here("results", "metrics", "final_rf_model.rds"))
saveRDS(final_metrics, here("results", "metrics", "final_rf_metrics.rds"))

message("Random Forest pipeline complete.")
```


# Support Vector Machine
```{r}
library(tidymodels)
library(tidyverse)
library(finetune) 
library(furrr)
library(here)

plan(multisession, workers = parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE))
options(future.globals.maxSize = 3000 * 1024^2)


# Settings

tune_prop <- 0.1        # share of training data used for tuning
final_fit_prop <- 1     # share of training data used for the final fit
use_cache <- TRUE       # cache fitted results as .rds files in results/metrics
cache_dir <- here("results", "metrics")
output_dir <- here("results", "metrics", "svm")


# Helpers

cached <- function(file, expr) {
  path <- file.path(cache_dir, file)
  if (use_cache && file.exists(path)) return(readRDS(path))
  result <- expr
  if (use_cache) saveRDS(result, path)
  result
}

# kernlab cannot combine class.weights with prob.model = TRUE.
# Weighted probabilities are made from the unweighted probability

reweight_probs <- function(preds, weights) {
  p <- sweep(as.matrix(preds[prob_cols]), 2, weights[lv], `*`)
  p <- p / rowSums(p)
  preds[prob_cols] <- as.data.frame(p)
  preds$.pred_class <- factor(lv[max.col(p, ties.method = "first")],
    levels = lv)
  preds
}

# kernlab bug: when its Platt line search stops early it prints
# "line search fails A B ..." and stores a vector instead of list(A, B) for
# that class pair, which breaks predict().

fit_with_platt_repair <- function(wf, data) {
  log <- capture.output(fitted <- fit(wf, data))
  pm <- extract_fit_engine(fitted)@prob.model
  broken <- which(!map_lgl(pm, is.list))
  if (length(broken) == 0) return(fitted)

  fails <- str_match_all(paste(log, collapse = " "),
    "line search fails\\s+(\\S+)\\s+(\\S+)")[[1]]
  stopifnot(nrow(fails) == length(broken))
  for (k in seq_along(broken)) {
    pm[[broken[k]]] <- list(A = as.numeric(fails[k, 2]),
      B = as.numeric(fails[k, 3]))
  }
  fitted$fit$fit$fit@prob.model <- pm
  message("Repaired Platt parameters for class pair(s): ",
    paste(broken, collapse = ", "))
  fitted
}

# Precision, recall and F1 for each class (one class vs the rest).
per_class_table <- function(preds) {
  map_dfr(lv, \(cl) {
    truth <- factor(preds$damage_grade == cl, levels = c(TRUE, FALSE))
    est <- factor(preds$.pred_class == cl, levels = c(TRUE, FALSE))
    tibble(class = cl,
      precision = precision_vec(truth, est),
      recall = recall_vec(truth, est),
      f1 = f_meas_vec(truth, est))
  })
}


# Data

if (!file.exists(here("data", "processed", "earthquake.rds"))) {
  source(here("shared", "01_data_setup.R"))
}
split_path <- here("data", "processed", "split_data.RData")
if (!file.exists(split_path)) {
  source(here("shared", "02_preprocessing.R"))
}
load(split_path)

lv <- levels(train_data$damage_grade)
prob_cols <- paste0(".pred_", lv)

set.seed(1)
tune_data <- training(initial_split(train_data, prop = tune_prop,
  strata = damage_grade))
set.seed(1)
resamples <- vfold_cv(tune_data, v = 5, strata = damage_grade)

# Class weights by inverse class frequency.
class_counts <- count(train_data, damage_grade)
class_weights <- setNames(
  nrow(train_data) / (nrow(class_counts) * class_counts$n),
  as.character(class_counts$damage_grade))

# Metrics
qwk <- metric_tweak("qwk", kap, weighting = "quadratic")
f_macro <- metric_tweak("f_macro", f_meas, estimator = "macro")
f_micro <- metric_tweak("f_micro", f_meas, estimator = "micro")
report_metrics <- metric_set(qwk, f_macro, f_micro, bal_accuracy, accuracy,
  roc_auc)


# Models
# Tuning runs without the probability model (prob.model = FALSE), models are selected by QWK, which only needs
# class predictions.

make_svm_wf <- function(kernel, weighted, prob = FALSE) {
  spec <- switch(kernel,
    rbf = svm_rbf(mode = "classification", rbf_sigma = tune(), cost = tune()),
    linear = svm_linear(mode = "classification", cost = tune()),
    poly = svm_poly(mode = "classification", cost = tune(), degree = 2,
      scale_factor = tune()))
  engine_args <- list(prob.model = prob, cache = 1000, tol = 0.01)
  if (weighted) engine_args$class.weights <- class_weights
  spec <- do.call(set_engine, c(list(spec, "kernlab"), engine_args))
  workflow() |> add_model(spec) |> add_recipe(base_recipe)
}

make_params <- function(kernel, wf) {
  params <- extract_parameter_set_dials(wf)
  switch(kernel,
    rbf = params |>
      update(rbf_sigma = rbf_sigma(c(-4, -1)), cost = cost(c(-2, 3))),
    linear = params |> update(cost = cost(c(-2, 3))),
    poly = params |> update(cost = cost(c(-2, 3))))
}

grid_size <- c(rbf = 20, linear = 10, poly = 20)


# Tuning
# Racing evaluates a in parallel and drops candidates that
# are significantly worse after the first 3 folds.

model_names <- c("rbf_none", "rbf_weighted", "linear_none",
  "linear_weighted", "poly_none", "poly_weighted")

tune_results <- list()
for (m in model_names) {
  kernel <- str_remove(m, "_.*")
  wf <- make_svm_wf(kernel, weighted = str_detect(m, "weighted"))
  set.seed(1)
  tune_results[[m]] <- cached(paste0("svm_race_", m, "_v4.rds"),
    tune_race_anova(wf, resamples = resamples, grid = grid_size[[kernel]],
      param_info = make_params(kernel, wf), metrics = metric_set(qwk),
      control = control_race(save_pred = TRUE,
        parallel_over = "everything")))
}

# Best CV QWK of each model; the highest is selected.
qwk_by_model <- imap_dfr(tune_results, \(res, m)
  show_best(res, metric = "qwk", n = 1) |> mutate(model = m)) |>
  arrange(desc(mean))
qwk_by_model |> select(model, mean, std_err)

best_model <- qwk_by_model$model[1]
best_kernel <- str_remove(best_model, "_.*")
best_weighted <- str_detect(best_model, "weighted")
best_parameter <- select_best(tune_results[[best_model]], metric = "qwk")
param_tag <- best_parameter |>
  select(-.config) |>
  unlist() |>
  signif(3) |>
  paste(collapse = "_")


# Selected model: CV with probabilities
# Refitted with the probability model (always unweighted, see
# reweight_probs()) for ROC AUC. The raw predictions are the unweighted
# baseline; the reweighted ones are the selected model.

best_prob_wf <- make_svm_wf(best_kernel, weighted = FALSE, prob = TRUE) |>
  finalize_workflow(best_parameter)

svm_cv <- cached(
  paste0("svm_cv_best_prob_", best_kernel, "_", param_tag, "_v5.rds"),
  fit_resamples(best_prob_wf, resamples, metrics = report_metrics,
    control = control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE)))

baseline_preds <- collect_predictions(svm_cv)
cv_preds <- if (best_weighted) {
  reweight_probs(baseline_preds, class_weights)
} else {
  baseline_preds
}


# Final model and holdout predictions

set.seed(1)
final_data <- if (final_fit_prop < 1) {
  training(initial_split(train_data, prop = final_fit_prop,
    strata = damage_grade))
} else {
  train_data
}

final_fit <- cached(
  paste0("svm_final_model_", best_kernel, "_", param_tag, "_",
    final_fit_prop, "_v6.rds"),
  fit_with_platt_repair(best_prob_wf, final_data))

# Prediction cost grows with the number of support vectors, so the holdout
# set is predicted in parallel chunks.
holdout_preds <- test_data |>
  split(ceiling(seq_len(nrow(test_data)) / 5000)) |>
  future_map(\(d) augment(final_fit, new_data = d),
    .options = furrr_options(packages = c("tidymodels", "kernlab"))) |>
  bind_rows()
plan(sequential)

if (best_weighted) {
  holdout_preds <- reweight_probs(holdout_preds, class_weights)
}


# Saved outputs

dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

summarise_cv <- function(preds, label) {
  preds |>
    group_by(id) |>
    report_metrics(truth = damage_grade, all_of(prob_cols),
      estimate = .pred_class) |>
    group_by(.metric) |>
    summarize(mean = mean(.estimate),
      std_err = sd(.estimate) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(model = label, .before = 1)
}

selected_label <- paste0(
  if (best_weighted) "Class-weighted " else "Unweighted ",
  toupper(best_kernel), " SVM (",
  best_parameter |>
    select(-.config) |>
    imap_chr(\(v, p) paste(p, signif(v, 3))) |>
    paste(collapse = ", "),
  ")")

outputs <- list(
  cv_metrics = bind_rows(
    summarise_cv(baseline_preds, "Unweighted baseline"),
    summarise_cv(cv_preds, selected_label)),
  cv_per_class_metrics = per_class_table(cv_preds),
  best_parameters = best_parameter,
  holdout_metrics = report_metrics(holdout_preds, truth = damage_grade,
    all_of(prob_cols), estimate = .pred_class),
  per_class_metrics = per_class_table(holdout_preds))

iwalk(outputs, \(table, name) {
  print(table)
  write_csv(table, file.path(output_dir, paste0(name, ".csv")))
})

report_metrics         
summarise_cv(cv_preds, "check") 
read_csv(file.path(output_dir, "cv_metrics.csv"))
```

# Shared Cross-Validation Comparison

The table below compares the frozen candidate models using training-set
cross-validation results only. Quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) is the primary
selection metric. Macro F1 and macro recall provide supporting evidence about
performance across all three damage classes, while accuracy summarizes overall
classification performance.

```{r}
#| label: shared-cv-model-comparison
#| echo: false

cv_model_comparison <- readr::read_csv(
  here::here("results", "metrics", "shared_cv_model_comparison.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

cv_model_comparison |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      c(qwk, macro_f1, accuracy, macro_recall),
      ~ scales::number(.x, accuracy = 0.0001)
    )
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Model", "QWK", "Macro F1", "Accuracy", "Macro Recall", "Status"
    ),
    caption = "Five-fold training cross-validation comparison of frozen model candidates."
  )
```

The geographic elastic net and XGBoost currently have nearly identical QWK
values. The difference is too small to treat either model as clearly superior
without considering variation across folds and class-specific performance.
Random-forest results remain pending because comparable cross-validation
metrics have not yet been committed to the repository. No holdout results are
used in this comparison or for final candidate selection.
